questions.q: Why was the decision threshold chosen using out-of-fold predictions on the training set rather than on the test set?
options: Out-of-fold predictions are more accurate than test predictions
The test set has no labels
Choosing it on the test set would leak information and make the final estimate optimistic
scikit-learn cannot score a threshold on a test set
questions.explain: Every decision made with the test set uses up its role as an untouched, honest estimate. Out-of-fold scores let you tune the threshold using training data only.

questions.q: An offer costs 10 and a missed cancellation costs 100. If an offer always saves the customer, above what cancel probability does contacting the customer pay off?
questions.explain: Contact when p x 100 > 10, so p > 10/100 = 0.10. The empirically chosen threshold, 0.11, agreed with this.

questions.q: At threshold 0.11 the test confusion matrix was [[695, 372], [43, 90]]. What are the recall and precision for cancellers?
questions.explain: Recall = 90 / (90 + 43) = 0.677. Precision = 90 / (90 + 372) = 0.195. The low precision is the price of catching two-thirds of cancellers when misses are so costly.

questions.q: The test average precision (0.333) was higher than the cross-validated 0.258, and the bootstrap interval was 0.26 to 0.418. How should you report this?
options: Report 0.333 alone, since the test set is the truth
Report the interval and the cross-validated figure, noting that only 133 positives make the test score noisy
Retrain the model until the test score matches cross-validation
questions.explain: A small test set gives a noisy point estimate. Presenting the interval and the more conservative cross-validation number is the honest, defensible summary.

questions.q: Which of these is an honest limitation to state in the model card for this capstone?
options: The model finds associations, not causes, and the data is synthetic
The model cannot be saved with joblib
The test set was used for tuning
questions.explain: Synthetic data, non-causal associations, the optimistic save-rate assumption, no time axis, and a small test set are all real limits. The other options are false for this project.
